question: Which moral theories do your answers to ten trolley cases match, and where do those answers pull against each other?
finding: Six theories written as rules agree on only one of the ten cases, and of the 1,024 possible sets of answers only 46 never permit a harder case while forbidding an easier one and also answer the two identically coded cases alike.
limit: Ten yes-or-no answers to coded thought experiments cannot identify the theory a person holds, and the coding of each case is itself contestable.
